answer: Credit follows dependence, not self-assertion: a claim earns nothing until unrelated heads' accepted work stands on it, each stand re-checked with the claim withheld - if the dependent work stops holding, the citation voids the claim. A farm cannot cite its siblings and its internal bridge collapses as one, so every extra head needs strangers' work leaning on it. That input is the crowd's work at risk: one head's reward backs only so many claims, and the tide of dependants thins as a cluster grows. The kernel of a claim is its dependants, so clones supply claims, not dependants.
